items.prose: A master ropemaker executed a 72-diameter long splice on a 1.75-inch cotton transmission rope, replacing individual strands so that the outside diameter remained completely uniform. The seamless joint ran through 1,800 RPM grooved sheaves without a whisper or bump.

Machining 45-degree angular V-grooves into the cast-iron flywheels allowed the 2-inch transmission ropes to wedge firmly against the groove flanks without bottoming out. The wedge friction transmitted 120 kW to the main intake fan with zero belt slippage.

Four-strand Lambeth power ropes spun from extra-long staple Egyptian cotton fiber exhibited superior internal flexibility over Manila cordage. The soft cotton core absorbed torsional engine pulses from the single-cylinder gas engine without throwing loops.

Applying a hot compound of beeswax, flake graphite, and tallow to the power ropes dissipated high-voltage electrostatic charges generated by sheave friction. The conductive coating eliminated static spark hazards across the flour mill milling bays.

Persistent wet-weather stretching in the continuous single-rope drive loop caused the suspended 800-kg tension carriage to hit the bottom track limit stops. The loss of take-up tension caused the slack rope to jump out of the idler sheave groove.

Unequal wear in the cast-iron sheave grooves changed effective pitch diameters by up to 3mm across the ten-groove bank. The resulting differential linear speed forced tighter ropes to slip and squeal violently, generating scorching surface temperatures.

Tucking a five-tuck eye splice around a heavy galvanized cast steel thimble with double annealed iron wire throat seizing created an indestructible terminal loop. Destructive proof-loading to 35 tons failed to deform the thimble or slip the splice tucks.
